content.value_statement: Investors often have data but lack a consistent framework for comparing business quality, valuation, growth, and risk. This skill routes the question to a suitable investor lens and grounds the analysis in dated LLMQuant Data.
actual_capabilities: Routes a question to a named investor workflow using the requested asset, horizon, and decision type.
Structures analysis around valuation, competitive advantage, growth, leverage, catalysts, or downside risk.
Uses LLMQuant Data for filings, prices, fundamentals, ownership, macro indicators, and related evidence.
Separates retrieved facts, user assumptions, and framework-based interpretation.
Reports missing data, observation dates, stale-data notices, and uncertainty when relevant.
limitations: It does not guarantee investment returns or predict market prices.
It depends on the availability, coverage, and freshness of LLMQuant Data.
It does not replace professional financial, tax, or legal advice.
It does not independently verify information outside retrieved or user-provided evidence.

use_cases.title: Screen a Candidate
use_cases.description: Compare a company with a value, quality, growth, or compounder framework using dated fundamentals and valuation evidence.

use_cases.title: Stress-Test a Thesis
use_cases.description: Use downside, inversion, cycle, or tail-risk questions to identify assumptions that could invalidate an existing investment thesis.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Investment Memo
use_cases.description: Create a concise evidence-led memo with a selected lens, explicit assumptions, key risks, and a defined decision signal.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Lens
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [company or asset] using the most suitable investor lens. State the lens, decision horizon, signal, evidence, and main uncertainty.

prompt_templates.title: Value a Business
prompt_templates.prompt: Use a value-investing workflow to assess [company]. Review earnings quality, balance-sheet strength, valuation, margin of safety, and evidence dates.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Growth
prompt_templates.prompt: Use a growth or innovation lens for [company]. Test growth durability, reinvestment, addressable market, operating leverage, valuation, and downside cases.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Frameworks
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate [company or asset] through [three named lenses]. Separate retrieved facts from interpretation, reconcile conflicting signals, and recommend the next evidence to collect.

output_examples.input: Assess a durable consumer business with a long holding period.
output_examples.output: Selected lens: long-term owner. Review moat, pricing power, management, reinvestment, valuation, and margin of safety. Signal: watch until valuation evidence supports the thesis.

output_examples.input: Stress-test a high-growth company priced for rapid expansion.
output: Growth case: expansion remains durable if revenue, margins, and market adoption meet the stated assumptions.
Risk case: slower adoption or higher funding costs can reduce intrinsic value materially.
Next evidence: verify recent filings, operating metrics, valuation inputs, and observation dates.

output_examples.input: Compare a value lens with a macro lens for an equity position.
output_examples.output: The value lens emphasizes business quality and price. The macro lens emphasizes liquidity, cycle position, and sizing. The decision should state which evidence conflicts and which missing input matters most.

best_practices: Name the asset, horizon, decision type, and preferred lens before requesting analysis.
Ask for dated evidence and keep retrieved facts separate from interpretation.
Treat every signal as a research input, then verify assumptions before acting.
anti_patterns: Do not present a persona-style opinion without identifying the supporting evidence.
Do not treat a workflow signal as a guarantee, forecast, or personalized recommendation.
Do not fill missing prices, filings, ownership data, or valuation inputs with guesses.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It routes investment questions to analytical workflows based on established investor frameworks and LLMQuant Data.

faq.question: Which investor lenses are available?
faq.answer: Available lenses cover value, quality, growth, innovation, macro, activism, cycles, tail risk, and other defined approaches.

faq.question: What data does it use?
faq.answer: It can use LLMQuant Data for filings, fundamentals, prices, ownership, macro indicators, valuation inputs, and related research.

faq.question: Can it provide a buy or sell recommendation?
faq.answer: It can produce a framework-specific signal, but it does not provide guaranteed outcomes or replace professional financial advice.

faq.question: How should I handle missing data?
faq.answer: The workflow should name the missing input and continue only with retrieved evidence or assumptions explicitly supplied by the user.

faq.question: Does it execute commands or access my environment?
faq.answer: The skill content defines analytical workflows and data requirements. Its documented workflow does not instruct command execution or environment-variable access.
